tasks.title: D22 Phase 2 — IBKR contract-details request/callback plumbing (bridge signals + client overrides + MarketDataManager) [baseline record; AC-D22.2.3 corrected by D23.1]
tasks.description: Add the new reqContractDetails path: IBBridge.contract_details(int, object) and contract_details_end(int) signals; IBApiClient.contractDetails/contractDetailsEnd overrides that call super() and forward to those signals (mirroring historicalData/historicalDataEnd); MarketDataManager.req_contract_details(contract) -> int (id_manager.get_id() + pacing_manager.throttle() + client.reqContractDetails) and cancel_contract_details(req_id) — a capability-guarded best-effort cancel (getattr(self.client, 'cancelContractDetails', None), called only if present; None-safe; containment preserved), as corrected by D23.1 / AC-D23.1.4. Add tests/test_ibkr_contract_details_d22.py; existing callbacks and their tests stay unchanged. [status done — carried as the corrected AC-D22.2.3 record.]
acceptance_criteria: AC-D22.2.1 (bridge signals) — Given IBBridge, Then it exposes a contract_details signal with signature (int, object) and a contract_details_end signal with signature (int).

AC-D22.2.2 (client overrides forward) — Given an IBApiClient with a bridge, When contractDetails(reqId, contractDetails) fires, Then super().contractDetails is invoked and bridge.contract_details is emitted with (reqId, contractDetails); When contractDetailsEnd(reqId) fires, Then super().contractDetailsEnd is invoked and bridge.contract_details_end is emitted with (reqId).

AC-D22.2.3 (manager request/cancel) [CORRECTED by D23.1 / AC-D23.1.4] — Given MarketDataManager, When req_contract_details(contract) is called, Then it returns a reqId allocated by id_manager.get_id(), calls pacing_manager.throttle() once, and calls client.reqContractDetails(reqId, contract); When cancel_contract_details(req_id) is called, Then it is a capability-guarded best-effort cancel — it resolves client.cancelContractDetails via getattr(self.client, 'cancelContractDetails', None) and calls it only when present (the pinned ibapi 9.81.1.post1 has no EClient.cancelContractDetails, so on the pinned surface it is a clean no-op that neither raises nor silently swallows an AttributeError), passing None or a client whose present cancel raises does not propagate an exception, and the method documents the pinned-ibapi absence, TWS's own contractDetailsEnd/error termination, and ContractLookupService's local invalidation (bounded QTimer + cancel_all) as the safety net. [This supersedes the former 'calls client.cancelContractDetails(req_id)' mandate; D22's feature criteria are not reopened.]
AC-D22.2.4 (existing callbacks unchanged) — Given the existing historical/RT tick callbacks, When the new overrides are added, Then their forwarding behaviour and existing tests are unchanged.

tests.description: Import IBBridge and assert it has contract_details and contract_details_end attributes that are bound signals, and that a sentinel object round-trips through contract_details.
tests.expected_result: IBBridge exposes the two new contract-details signals with the expected payloads.

tests.description: Construct an IBApiClient (or a harness with the EWrapper methods) with a spy bridge and a spy super() path; call client.contractDetails(11, cd) and client.contractDetailsEnd(11); assert bridge.contract_details received (11, cd) and contract_details_end received 11, with each super() call made.
tests.expected_result: Both EWrapper overrides invoke super() and forward the identical args to the bridge signals.

tests.description: With a fake client and monkeypatched id_manager/pacing_manager, call MarketDataManager.req_contract_details(contract); assert the returned id is the allocated id, throttle was called, and client.reqContractDetails received (id, contract). Then [corrected by D23.1 / AC-D23.1.4] call cancel_contract_details(id): for a client that does NOT define cancelContractDetails (a types.SimpleNamespace(reqContractDetails=...), the pinned-ibapi shape) it completes with no exception; for a spy client that DOES define it, it is invoked once with id (cancel_calls == [id]); call cancel_contract_details(None) and assert no call; and with a present-but-raising client assert no exception escapes.
tests.expected_result: req_contract_details allocates, throttles and delegates; cancel_contract_details is capability-guarded (missing capability -> clean no-op, present -> called once with req_id), None-safe and containment-preserving (a raising present cancel does not propagate).

tasks.title: D23 Phase 1 — capability-guarded, documented contract-details cancel (D23.1 / ESC-030)
tasks.description: Rewrite MarketDataManager.cancel_contract_details in ibkr/market_data.py: keep the `if req_id is None: return` no-op; resolve `cancel = getattr(self.client, 'cancelContractDetails', None)` and call it only if present, inside the retained containment (try/except Exception: pass); add a docstring/comment documenting that (a) the pinned ibapi 9.81.1.post1 exposes no EClient.cancelContractDetails, (b) TWS's own contractDetailsEnd/error ends the wire reqContractDetails request, and (c) ContractLookupService's local invalidation (bounded QTimer + cancel_all on disconnect) is the real safety net. req_contract_details is unchanged. Extend tests/test_ibkr_contract_details_d22.py: add the pre-fix-red code-shape/source assertion, a missing-capability behavioural post-fix guard, and keep the present-method/None/raising cases.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D23.1.1 (capability-guarded cancel — no raised/swallowed AttributeError) — Given a MarketDataManager whose client lacks cancelContractDetails (the pinned ibapi 9.81.1.post1 shape), When cancel_contract_details(req_id) is called, Then it returns without raising and without touching a missing attribute (no AttributeError occurs at all — the bare self.client.cancelContractDetails(...) access is gone and the method is resolved via getattr(self.client, 'cancelContractDetails', None), called only if present); Given a client that does expose cancelContractDetails, When called, Then that method is invoked exactly once with req_id.

AC-D23.1.2 (documented absence + safety net) — Given the source of cancel_contract_details, Then its comment/docstring names the three facts: the pinned ibapi 9.81.1.post1 exposes no EClient.cancelContractDetails; the wire-side reqContractDetails is ended by TWS's own contractDetailsEnd/error; and ContractLookupService's local invalidation (bounded QTimer + cancel_all on disconnect) is the real safety net.

AC-D23.1.3 (None-safe + containment preserved) — Given req_id is None, Then the method is a no-op that calls nothing; Given a client whose (present) capability-guarded cancel raises, Then no exception escapes.

tests.description: Pre-fix-red code-shape/source assertion (the Q8 evidence for D23.1): ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(inspect.getsource(MarketDataManager.cancel_contract_details))) and assert (a) no ast.Attribute node with attr == 'cancelContractDetails' (equivalently the substring 'self.client.cancelContractDetails(' is absent — the bare unguarded access is gone) AND (b) the capability guard getattr(self.client, "cancelContractDetails", None) is present in the source. Red against the current file (bare access at ibkr/market_data.py:82, no getattr), green after the guard.
tests.expected_result: Pre-fix red (bare self.client.cancelContractDetails(...) present; getattr guard absent); post-fix green (no bare attribute access; the getattr(..., None) capability guard present). This is the ONLY genuine pre-fix-red check for D23.1.

tests.description: Post-fix guard (explicitly NOT pre-fix-red): build a client that does not define cancelContractDetails (types.SimpleNamespace(reqContractDetails=lambda *a: None), the pinned-ibapi shape) and call MarketDataManager(client).cancel_contract_details(7); assert it returns with no exception. It passes on both the pre- and post-fix trees (the retained try/except already swallows the pre-fix AttributeError), so it documents the intended no-op and guards a regression that removes both the guard and the containment.
tests.expected_result: On the pinned-ibapi shape the call completes with no exception raised or surfaced.

tests.description: Post-fix guard: with the method-defining _FakeClient spy, call MarketDataManager(client).cancel_contract_details(7) and assert the method was invoked exactly once with req_id (client.cancel_calls == [7]).
tests.expected_result: When the client exposes cancelContractDetails it is called exactly once with req_id.

tests.description: Assert the source of cancel_contract_details (docstring/comment) names the three documented facts: the pinned '9.81.1.post1' ibapi absence, TWS's 'contractDetailsEnd' (and error) termination of the wire request, and 'ContractLookupService' local invalidation with 'cancel_all'.
tests.expected_result: The method's comment/docstring contains the pinned-version absence, the TWS contractDetailsEnd/error termination, and the ContractLookupService (bounded QTimer + cancel_all) safety net.

tests.description: Review confirmation (the requirement's 'review-verified' measurable) that cancel_contract_details documents, accurately and completely, that the pinned ibapi 9.81.1.post1 exposes no EClient.cancelContractDetails, that TWS ends the reqContractDetails request via contractDetailsEnd/error, and that ContractLookupService's local invalidation is the safety net.
tests.expected_result: A reviewer confirms the three named facts appear in the method's comment/docstring.

tests.description: Call MarketDataManager(spy_client).cancel_contract_details(None) and assert it is a no-op: the client's cancel method is never called.
tests.expected_result: req_id is None returns immediately without invoking the client.

tests.description: With a client whose present cancelContractDetails raises RuntimeError, call cancel_contract_details(7) and assert no exception escapes (the containment try/except Exception: pass is preserved).
tests.expected_result: A raising present-method cancel is contained and does not propagate.

tasks.title: D23 Phase 2 — remove_symbol drops the removed row's _row_data key (D23.2 / ESC-031)
tasks.description: In ui/watchlist_panel.py::WatchlistPanel.remove_symbol, drop the removed row's own _row_data entry while re-indexing — e.g. self._row_data.pop(row, None) before the existing `{(r-1 if r > row else r): values ...}` re-map — so that after remove_symbol returns True, set(self._row_data.keys()) == set(range(self.table.rowCount())) (no stale key), while _req_to_row values and _flash_timers keys cover exactly the surviving rows. Update the remove_symbol docstring to state the invariant. _prev_close/_last_price (reqId-keyed) and the add_symbol/clear paths are unchanged. Extend tests/test_watchlist_add_remove_d22.py with the missing last-row (and/or first/only-row) coverage that is red pre-fix.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D23.2.1 (no stale row key — last-row removal) — Given a panel with n >= 2 rows, When the last row's symbol is removed, Then table.rowCount() == n-1 AND set(_row_data.keys()) == set(range(n-1)) (the removed row's key is dropped, not merely overwritten by a later key). Measurable: a 3-row panel, remove_symbol(last) -> sorted(_row_data.keys()) == [0, 1].

AC-D23.2.2 (first / middle / only-row removal) — Given a panel with rows, When the first, a middle, or the only row's symbol is removed, Then set(_row_data.keys()) == set(range(table.rowCount())) in every case (only-row case -> rowCount() == 0 and _row_data == {}). The same invariant holds for _req_to_row values and _flash_timers keys (no key for a removed row survives).

AC-D23.2.3 (coverage added) — Given the D22-05 remove tests, Then a last-row (and/or first-row / only-row) removal assertion is added so the stale-key branch is actually covered — the existing middle-row check (test_D22_05_T02) passes even with the defect and cannot be the only guard. Measurable: the new assertion fails against the pre-fix remove_symbol and passes after the fix.

AC-D23.2.4 (regression) — Given the fix, Then test_D22_05_T02 (middle-row re-index, reqId cancellation, flash-timer re-index, later-tick routing) and test_D22_05_T03 (absent/blank no-op) remain green, and _row_data remains a valid dict for _rebuild_table/_set_cell after any removal (cached FieldKey-bound values are not shifted onto the wrong row).

tests.description: Pre-fix-red last-row removal: a 3-row panel (AAPL/MSFT/TSLA) with reqIds 1/2/3; remove_symbol('TSLA') -> assert table.rowCount() == 2 and set(_row_data.keys()) == set(range(2)) (sorted == [0, 1]); the removed row's key 2 is dropped, not merely overwritten. Red against the current remove_symbol (stale key 2).
tests.expected_result: Last-row removal leaves _row_data keyed exactly over the 2 surviving rows (pre-fix: stale key 2 present -> red; post-fix green).

tests.description: First/middle/only-row removal invariant: for a panel with rows, remove the first row (set(_row_data.keys()) == set(range(rowCount()))), a middle row (same), and the only row (rowCount() == 0 and _row_data == {}); in each case also assert the _req_to_row values and _flash_timers keys cover exactly the surviving rows and no removed row's reqId/timer key survives.
tests.expected_result: Every removal leaves _row_data keys, _req_to_row values and _flash_timers keys exactly over the surviving rows.

tests.description: Confirm the newly added last-row (and/or first/only-row) assertion is red against the pre-fix remove_symbol and green after the fix — e.g. by running the new assertion against the pre-fix revision (git stash / checked-out pre-fix tree) and recording both results; the existing middle-row check alone does not catch it.
tests.expected_result: The new assertion fails on the pre-fix remove_symbol (stale last-row key) and passes after the fix.

tests.description: Run test_D22_05_T02 (middle-row: reqId cancellation, _req_to_row/_prev_close/_last_price/flash-timer re-index, later-tick routing to the correct symbol row) and test_D22_05_T03 (absent/blank no-op) and assert they remain green after the fix.
tests.expected_result: The existing middle-row re-index and absent/blank no-op tests stay green.

tests.description: After a first-row and a last-row removal, assert _row_data is still a valid dict whose values stay FieldKey-bound and that _rebuild_table() and _set_cell(row, field, value) still resolve the correct symbol row (no shift of cached values onto the wrong row; DG32 binding preserved).
tests.expected_result: _row_data remains valid for _rebuild_table/_set_cell after any removal; cached field values stay bound to their symbol.

The offscreen pytest suite intermittently reports spurious failures because `tests/conftest.py` seeds a **single shared on-disk SQLite DB** at `tempfile.gettempdir()/tos_charting_test.sqlite3`, so concurrent/interleaved runs contend on it. All such failures pass in isolation and in a clean full-suite run — but always re-run the full suite to confirm before declaring green.

The offscreen suite occasionally reports a full-suite **SIGSEGV** (exit 139) at `tests/test_session_overlay.py::panel` and/or order-dependent `ModuleNotFoundError: tests.test_watchlist`, triggered by collection-order changes from new test files. Both are non-deterministic and pre-existing — confirm with a clean full-suite run before treating them as regressions.
